Let \(S=[ABC]\), \(AC=b\), and \(BC=a\).  
By the Angle Bisector Theorem,
\[
\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{7}{b}.
\]
The three equal-area regions are \(\triangle ABD\), quadrilateral \(ADFE\), and \(\triangle CEF\). Thus
\[
[ABD]=\frac S3,\qquad [CAD]=[ADFE]+[CEF]=\frac{2S}{3}.
\]
Since \(\triangle ABD\) and \(\triangle CAD\) share the same altitude from \(A\),
\[
\frac{[ABD]}{[CAD]}=\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{7}{b}.
\]
So
\[
\frac{7}{b}=\frac{S/3}{2S/3}=\frac12,
\]
giving \(b=14\).

Now triangle inequality with sides \(7,14,a\) gives
\[
14-7<a<14+7 \implies 7<a<21.
\]
Thus the integral values of \(BC=a\) are
\[
8,9,\ldots,20,
\]
which are \(13\) values.

\[
\boxed{13}
\]
